title: Two-level mall corridor with food stands selling ridiculously expensive muffins
content: First time posting but I wanted to see if anyone else had been to a similar place! I’ve been to this place a couple of times, but only ever visited the second floor which (so far) exists of a café. I usually am always having to go somewhere and only buy hot tea or similar to go. It’s a very cozy place, dimly lit with soft seats and kinda cramped but not to the point where it feels claustrophobic. If you want to get any of the more elaborate drinks you have to be there before a certain time or that section of the café closes and you’ll have to make do with more basic (but still very good) drinks. The first floor (or main floor? So far there aren’t more floors) is very lively with tons of people walking past or browsing different food stands. Think of it as a rather wide corridor with both sides full of food/baked goods vendors. In the middle are two kitchen-isle like tables with muffins piled high and low. I’ve never been to the first floor before but tonight I ended up there and wanted to get some to try. Funnily enough it was the price that startled me awake: one muffin was 70$ and the second one ”only” 50$. No thank you, I think I’ll keep to the upstairs café and hopefully get there before their part-closing time. (The second floor café also seems to exist at the top of an off-limits lighthouse with very narrow stairs leading up. I’ve entered that way too before although sometimes there’s someone trying to enforce the whole off-limits part) Has anyone else had similar experiences, like items having a value tied to real life currencies?
